To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
four epitopic sites, including the S599 epitope in the S protein, the N66 epitope in the M protein, and two epitopes in the N protein, N371 and 385, were identified by screening synthesized peptides.

four epitopic sites, located in the structural proteins S, M, N of the SARS-corona-virus, and a peptide, N385, located in the COOH termini of the N protein were detected by screening the synthesized peptides.

the immunoreactivity of the SARS-corona-virus N protein with SARS serum was detected by synthesized peptides and that the COOH-terminal peptide of the N protein may be a useful diagnostic marker for SARS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of antigenic sites of the structural proteins of SARS-coronovirus, and the results may contribute to the development of diagnostic reagents and antiviral vaccines.
the immunoreactive synthetic peptides of severe acute respiratory coronavirus (SARS-CoV) and their potential for serologic assays of SARS-CoV.
the development of a rapid diagnostic method and a safe antivaccine for SARS coronavirus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peptides from the COOH terminal region of N protein, N371 and especially N385, appear to be immunogenic, which may be used for serodiagnosis of SARS.
the N protein of SARS-coronovirus has the most potential to be developed as a safe vaccine for the prevention of SARS.
the N385 peptide is a potential antigen for serologic detection of SARS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach for the identification of antigenic sites in SARS-coronaviral proteins.
the immunoreactivities of these peptides may provide the basis for developing serologic assays and a safe and effective antiviral vaccine.
the SARS-corona virus N protein, particularly its COOH-terminus, may be a promising antigenic target for vaccine development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the COOH termini of the SARS coronavirus N proteins are highly immunogenic.
the N385 peptide may be useful for the development of a diagnostic assay.
the COOH termini of the structural proteins, especially the N protein, of SARS coronavirus are the most important immunogenic epitopes.
